A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ItDPDM research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across the substantial reorganization; no material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and Lakh MIDI experiments, including likelihood measurements, cross-training comparisons, convergence curves, and denoising examples.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds synthetic-distribution experiments, multivariate evaluations, image/music quality measurements, and qualitative music analyses.

M1.justification: The defining Poisson corruption, PRL, observation normalization, and iterative sampling procedure are retained. v4 adds a concrete timestep-conditioned, three-layer ConditionalMLP denoiser for synthetic experiments (Section 5.1 and Appendix C.2), extending the architecture instantiations beyond v1's image and music networks without replacing the core framework.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained CIFAR-10 and Lakh MIDI coverage, v4 evaluates six synthetic count distributions, eight non-negative continuous distributions, independent bivariate extensions, and two correlated count models (Section 5.1 and Appendix C). These substantially expand distributional coverage and evaluation of joint dependencies. Figure 3 also adds a NYC Taxi distribution example.

E2.justification: v1's quantitative comparisons center on Gaussian DDPM/IDDPM, ITDiff, and noise/loss cross-training variants. v4 adds evaluated LTJ and D3PM comparators in image/music quality Tables 3–4, and LTJ in synthetic Tables 1 and 7–9. Their discussion or citation in v1 did not constitute these experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported real-data training changes from 50 to 600 epochs, and log-SNR sampling from 1,000 to 100 values (v1 Section 6.1/Appendix E; v4 Appendix B.1). New protocols include synthetic WD and empirical-PMF NLL, rest-excluded music evaluation, and image/audio quality metrics, with image quality assessed through low-SNR denoising. These reported settings do not establish that retained results were rerun. The 1,024-note music description already appeared in v1 Appendix E.1.

E4.justification: The original cross-training and denoising analyses remain. v4 adds the music likelihood comparison excluding rests, examples examining Monte Carlo approximation error, and piano-roll/pitch-distribution diagnostics discussing structure, outliers, and sparse regions (Table 2b, Section 4, Appendix B.5.1). Appendix C.5 additionally tests recovery of dependent count distributions.

E5.justification: v1 does not specify repeated-run evaluation or define uncertainty estimates. v4 reports five-run synthetic evaluations, standard-deviation reporting, and ten-resample bootstrap uncertainty for PMF/PDF estimates (Appendices C.2–C.5 and checklist item 7). These are newly documented statistical practices, not evidence of an increase over a known v1 run count.

E6.justification: The original CIFAR and full-data music likelihood entries are retained, but extensive new results appear. Rest-excluded music NLL is 1.41 for Gaussian+MSE versus 0.23 for ItDPDM (Table 2b). New PoissMix WD is 0.99 for ItDPDM versus 3.76 for DDPM and 1.21 for LTJ (Table 1). Rankings are mixed: Table 3 reports music FAD of 0.64 for ItDPDM versus 0.61 for D3PM. These are added comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: v4 Appendix F substantially repairs v1 Appendix C's central KL-derivative proof by including differentiation of the probability weights and proving a Poisson–Stein identity. Equation 19 restores the e^alpha Jacobian missing from v1's log-SNR expression. v4 also adds the converse proof for the Gamma-prior characterization and an explicit vector-channel extension. Most existing tail-bound and continuous-time derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The Poisson framework and exact likelihood identity remain central, but v4 expands the main claims to synthetic distribution recovery, robustness across distribution families, and competitive generation quality. v1 foregrounded up-to-80% NLL reductions and faster convergence on images/music. The novelty framing is also qualified: v4 Appendix H explicitly acknowledges that LTJ uses the same Poisson–Bregman loss form, emphasizing its different likelihood connection.

C2.justification: Beyond the proof-of-concept qualification already in v1, v4 explicitly discusses limited training, fixed logistic parameters, low-SNR image denoising instead of generation from pure noise, and untested conditional/OOD settings (Sections 5.4 and 6). It distinguishes the exact identity from the learned-denoiser bound and discusses continuous-NLL incompatibility and failures on skewed Beta distributions (Section 4 and Appendix C.4).

D1.justification: Appendices B–C add substantial reproducibility information: synthetic network/optimizer settings, density-estimation procedures, evaluation sample counts, and the MIDI-to-audio pipeline with spectrogram parameters. v4 also adds an implementation link. However, its first-page availability statement conflicts with the checklist's planned future release, so actual code availability is unresolved from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The short diffusion overview expands into substantive positioning against Blackout Diffusion, Beta Diffusion, SEDD, continuous-time discrete score models, blurring diffusion, and edge-preserving diffusion (Section 7 and Appendix K). Appendix H/Table 10 adds an extensive LTJ comparison and acknowledges the shared loss form. This changes research positioning beyond citation-format or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively rewritten and reorganized. v1's separate formulation/framework sections are consolidated, numerical and experimental details move into reorganized appendices, and existing pseudocode moves into the main text. Dedicated limitations, broader-impact, and checklist sections are added. The changes substantially alter exposition and navigation independently of the new experiments.

P2.justification: The main text switches from two columns to one. v4 redraws the diffusion taxonomy, replaces the image-sample grid, combines the original likelihood tables into Table 2, and assembles the original loss/convergence plots into Figure 7. Readable typeset algorithms replace appendix screenshots, while new distribution plots, piano rolls, histograms, and comparison tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important weaknesses in v1 through direct comparisons with discrete competitors, systematic distribution-level evaluation with uncertainty, explicit generation-quality limitations, and repair of the central pointwise KL derivation. These substantially strengthen the paper's support and assessability. Mathematical consistency remains incomplete: Equation 19's Jacobian is absent from Algorithm 1/Appendix A.2, and Table 10 reverses PRL's arguments relative to Equation 5. Those limitations qualify, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains.
